title: Elastic slot allocator for mixed-turn workloads with KV coalescence and GPU compact mode
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Design and implement an elastic slot allocation layer in the continuous batching scheduler that improves throughput and latency for mixed prompt/response length workloads. This work combines length-aware slot tenure, KV coalescence heuristics (to reduce KV cache fragmentation), and a GPU memory compact mode that briefly trades off scheduling concurrency for reduced slab fragmentation and defragmentation pressure. Goal is to reduce OOM incidents for mixed-turn traffic and improve 95th percentile tail latency without increasing average cost by more than 6%.
acceptance_criteria: New slot allocator can be toggled per deployment via runtime flag and defaults to off for backward compatibility
95th percentile latency for mixed-turn benchmark decreases by >= 10% compared to baseline continuous scheduler with same throughput
KV cache residency fragmentation metric reduces by >= 20% on synthetic skewed-dialog benchmark
End-to-end cost per token increases by <= 6% on average across benchmarks, or we provide a quantization of when to enable compact mode to stay within cost budget
No increase in production OOM incidents post-rolling deploy over a 48h soak compared to control group
steps: Prototype elastic slot allocator algorithm in Python simulator using production trace samples
Measure KV residency and fragmentation with different coalescence heuristics (age-based, length-clustered, prefix-affinity)
Implement C++/Rust scheduler-side change to expose slot tenure and eviction hints
Add GPU compact mode that: reduces concurrent slot count, triggers aggressive KV coalescence, and runs a light-weight slab defrag between bursts
Add feature flag and rollout toggle in control plane; wire up runtime metrics and dashboards
Run large-scale canary on dedicated pool with shadow traffic and collect latency/cost/oom metrics
Iterate heuristics based on canary results and prepare rollout playbook
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Raman: Created ticket after spike of OOMs during mixed-turn load test. Initial idea: combine slot tenancy policies with KV consolidation to reduce fragmentation.

2026-03-03 - Miguel Ortega: Built simulator harness and ran first sweep over three heuristics. Preliminary result: age-based coalescence reduces KV eviction churn but hurts short-turn latency during bursts.
2026-03-05 - Priya Shah (PM): Prioritize rollback safety. Add canary gating and automatic fallback to previous allocator if OOMs increase by >1 within 15m.
2026-03-07 - Elena Kim (SRE): Added dashboards to track KV_fragmentation_ratio, slot_utilization_by_length, slab_free_pct, and compact_mode_invocations. Suggested tracking GPU SM utilization impact.
2026-03-09 - Miguel Ortega: Implemented runtime flag and CPU-side prototype of the compact-mode defrag loop. Need review for locking semantics in scheduler loop.

2026-03-10 - Engineering review: Agreed to prefer prefix-affinity coalescence for customer-facing dialog workloads; combination with length-bucket aging gives best tradeoff in simulator runs. Next: integrate into C++ scheduler and bench on m60 and a100 pools.
decisions: Use prefix-affinity + length-bucketing as default KV coalescence heuristic after simulator experiments
Implement compact mode as an opt-in runtime flag with automatic canary gating and conservative defaults
Expose per-deployment tunables in Redwood Console for slot count cap, coalescence aggressiveness, and compact-mode window duration
